claim: For all integer partitions lam, mu, nu with at most 5 parts each, |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c^{lam}_{mu nu} > 0, every coefficient of the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} in the monomial basis is nonnegative (the rank-five rung of the King-Tollu-Toumazet conjecture, open; the rank-four rung is a theorem of Ferudun 2026).

quadruple.statement: For all integer partitions lam, mu, nu with at most 5 parts each, |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c^{lam}_{mu nu} > 0, every coefficient of the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} in the monomial basis is nonnegative (the rank-five rung of the King-Tollu-Toumazet conjecture, open; the rank-four rung is a theorem of Ferudun 2026).
quadruple.stage: Ehrhart theory of the hive polytopes of side 5, which are rational polytopes of dimension at most 6 in the space of the six interior hive entries, cut out by the rhombus inequalities whose 27 primitive normals form the set N_5 of 0/+-1 vectors of squared norm at most 4; the coefficients are localised by the McMullen Berline-Vergne formula on the transverse cones of faces, which are generated by subsets of N_5 for full-dimensional hives and by projections of N_5 otherwise, after the period-one dilation lemma transfers the lattice formula to the rational polytope

shape.objects: Triples with at most 5 parts and any size: an infinite set, but after localisation the objects that decide the claim are finite: the 27 primitive rhombus normals of N_5, the cone types they span (342 nonparallel pairs, C(27,3) = 2,925 triples, C(27,4) = 17,550 quadruples, C(27,5) = 80,730 quintuples, and their closures), and the projections of N_5 that carry the transverse cones of the non-full-dimensional hives. The hive polytope has dimension at most 6 and is rational, with vertex denominators above 1 already at rank 5.
shape.quantifiers: Universal over an infinite set of triples and over the coefficient index, but equivalent to a finite statement: every coefficient of every hive of rank 5 is nonnegative if the weight of the local formula is nonnegative on every cone type of the rank-5 atlas, one finite list per codimension, and the lists at codimensions 0 to 4 are settled.
shape.target_quantity: A decision. The value the runs produce is the minimum of the weight over each finite cone list, which is positive at codimensions 2, 3 and 4 (minima 1/9 at rank 4, 1/264 rank-uniform at codimension 3, 739/86400 for the closed rank-5 codimension-4 cones).
shape.ambient_structure: Polyhedral geometry (the hive polytope and its normal fan) together with valuation theory (McMullen local formulas, of which Berline-Vergne is one member of an affine family, with closed expressions known only in dimensions 2 and 3). The representation theory enters only through the hive theorem and the Horn factorisation.
shape.symmetries: The dihedral symmetry of the hive triangle acts on N_5 and hence on the cone atlas, so the finite lists are unions of orbits; c is symmetric in mu and nu; column addition keeps P and reduces the size, so the atlas is size-independent.
shape.configuration: The forbidden configuration is a negative coefficient; the required configuration on the proof side is a weight assignment, nonnegative on every cone of the rank-5 atlas and satisfying McMullen's balancing conditions. Unconditional relations: a_0 = 1, the top four coefficients of a full-dimensional hive are positive, and at rank 5 the coefficients of t^6 down to t^2 are positive.
shape.extremal_candidate: Two near-misses are recorded. On the polytope side, the hive polytopes with exactly D + 1 lattice points and normalized volume 2, whose coefficient ratios to the unimodular simplex are 24/25, 44/45 and 799/812 in dimensions 4, 5 and 6 (the box census of the sibling attack). On the weight side, the saturated four-normal cell of rank 5 with normal identifiers (0, 7, 23, 25) and weight -66821/2858240, which is negative and is not the full normal cone of any hive face; 132 of the 17,550 rank-5 four-normal cells are negative and each is repaired by slack closure.
shape.finite_certificates: The true side has a finite certificate: nonnegativity of the weight on the rank-5 codimension-5 cone list and on the projected atlases of the non-full-dimensional hives, or more weakly a solution y of the rank-5 instance of (HTE), a_q + partial_q^T y >= 0, which is a linear program over the finitely many cone types. The false side has a finite certificate: a five-part triple with a negative coefficient, which the box attack has excluded up to size 30 and the sampling of the sibling attack beyond it.
shape.monotonicity: Not monotone in the size: the atlas is size-free, so a rung is a statement about all sizes at once. The progress parameter is the codimension: codimensions 0 and 1 are volume and surface, 2 and 3 are settled rank-uniformly, 4 is settled at rank 5, and 5 is open; the coefficient of t^{6-q} is what codimension q controls.
shape.uniformity_parameter: The codimension q. The cone lists grow as C(27, q) with q, from 342 pairs to 80,730 quintuples, and the weight has a closed form only for q <= 3, so the cost of a rung is the weight in dimension q, not the enumeration.
shape.proof_shape: Enumerate the cone types at codimension 5, evaluate the weight exactly on each, and where a cell is negative apply the slack-closure step that either raises the normal rank or embeds the cell in a pointed rank-preserving closed superset whose weight is positive; then handle the non-full-dimensional hives by contracting to the intrinsic lattice and repeating on the projected atlas. The enabling step is an implementation of the Berline-Vergne weight in dimensions 4 and 5 by the defining local Euler-Maclaurin recursion, validated against the closed formulas in dimensions 2 and 3 and against Ehrhart polynomials of actual hive polytopes computed by Normaliz. Loss per step: none, the arithmetic is exact; the risk is that the negative cells at codimension 5 are not repairable by closure, which would be a barrier rather than a loss.
shape.neighbours: Rank 4, every coefficient: known true (Ferudun 2026, Theorem 1). Top four coefficients of full-dimensional hives of any rank: known true (Theorem 2). Rank 5 full-dimensional, coefficients of t^6 to t^2: known true (Theorem 3 and the codimension-four report). Rank 5 full-dimensional, the linear coefficient: open. Rank 5 non-full-dimensional of intrinsic dimension at least 3: open and explicitly not claimed there. Permutohedra: the analogous strong Berline-Vergne positivity is proved to dimension 6 and codimension 3 (Castillo-Liu) and the Ehrhart positivity it was meant to give is false for generalized permutohedra (Ferroni). Marked order polytopes: Ehrhart positive (Jochemko-Menon).
shape.known_bounds: Proved at rank 5: every coefficient of a non-full-dimensional hive of intrinsic dimension at most 2 (reciprocity); the coefficients of t^6, t^5, t^4, t^3 of a full-dimensional hive (rank-uniform, codimensions 0 to 3); the coefficient of t^2 (the codimension-4 atlas, 17,550 tuples, 903 nonsaturated with minimum 1/14400, 132 negative saturated cells each repaired, closed-cone minimum 739/86400). Verified by computation: no negative coefficient among the 1,334,669 five-part polynomials of size at most 30 (a theorem by two independent programs, the sibling box attack) and among 400,000 sampled five-part hives of sizes 31 to 200. Ceilings: no closed formula for the weight above dimension 3; termwise positivity of the weight is false at codimension 4, so a cell-by-cell argument fails; the codimension-4 script of the source is not distributed.
shape.missing_input: Two inputs. First, the value of the Berline-Vergne weight on the five-dimensional cones spanned by rank-5 rhombus normals, for which no closed formula is in print and no distributed implementation exists, together with the closure argument that repairs the negative cells. Second, the intrinsic-lattice contraction that turns the projected transverse cone of a non-full-dimensional five-part hive into a cone of the intrinsic lattice, so that the same atlas argument applies.
shape.base_theory: ZFC, and in fact primitive recursive arithmetic for the finite part: every step is exact rational arithmetic on integral Gram matrices and on rational cones, and the local Euler-Maclaurin recursion terminates in the dimension. No hypothesis beyond ZFC bears on the claim. Lean cannot state the claim: Mathlib has no Littlewood-Richardson coefficient, though the finite cone statements could be stated there.

known: P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} is a polynomial in t: Derksen and Weyman, J. Algebra 255 (2002) 247-257, doi:10.1016/S0021-8693(02)00125-4; Rassart, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 107 (2004) 161-179, arXiv:math/0308101 (also the chamber-wise polynomiality of the coefficients in (lam, mu, nu)); Thawinrak, arXiv:2211.06810.

c = the number of integer hives (lattice points of the hive polytope), and saturation: Knutson and Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999) 1055-1090, arXiv:math/9807160; the facets of the Littlewood-Richardson cone: Knutson, Tao, Woodward, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004) 19-48, arXiv:math/0107011.

The positivity conjecture and the factorisation on saturated Horn facets: King, Tollu, Toumazet, CRM Proc. Lecture Notes 34 (2004) 99-112, doi:10.1090/crmp/034/10; 'The hive model and the polynomial nature of stretched Littlewood-Richardson coefficients', Sem. Lothar. Combin. 54A (2006) B54Ad, https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~slc/wpapers/s54Akitoto1.pdf; J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 116 (2009) 314-333, doi:10.1016/j.jcta.2008.06.005; Cho, Jung, Moon, DMTCS Proc. (2008), doi:10.46298/dmtcs.3592, Theorem 1.3.

c = 1 implies P = 1: Knutson, Tao, Woodward 2004. c = 2 implies P = t + 1: Ikenmeyer, J. Algebraic Combin. 44 (2016) 1-29, arXiv:1209.1521; Sherman, doi:10.1016/j.jalgebra.2017.03.011, arXiv:1505.06551.

Positivity for all triples of length <= 4; the top four coefficients of every full-dimensional hive positive; full-dimensional 5-part hives positive except possibly the linear coefficient; termwise Berline-Vergne positivity fails at codimension 4 (a cell of weight -349/28800); the reduction of the general conjecture to the effectivity statement (HTE), which is <a_q, w> >= 0 for every nonnegative balanced realizable face weight w by rational Farkas duality; the strip construction realising 3 x N transportation polytopes as Littlewood-Richardson polytopes: Ferudun, arXiv:2607.22301 (2026-07-24), with the replay bundle github.com/AlperTheKing/ktt-positivity.

McMullen local formulas: each Ehrhart coefficient is a sum over faces of the relative volume weighted by a function of the normal cone alone, and the weights are far from unique: Ring and Schuermann, arXiv:1709.10390 (also Ring, arXiv:1812.06654). The Berline-Vergne valuation as a tool for Ehrhart positivity: Castillo and Liu, arXiv:1509.07884; Castillo, Liu, Nill, Paffenholz, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 160 (2018) 316-331, arXiv:1704.05532.

The same termwise-local-formula heuristic fails on neighbouring families: matroid polytopes and generalized permutohedra are NOT Ehrhart positive (Ferroni, arXiv:2105.04465, disproving De Loera-Haws-Koeppe and Castillo-Liu); order polytopes are positive up to dimension 13 (Liu, Xin, Zhang, arXiv:2412.07164) and not from dimension 14 (Liu and Tsuchiya, Adv. Appl. Math. 108 (2019), arXiv:1806.08403); smooth lattice polytopes with every possibly-negative coefficient negative exist in every dimension >= 3 (Castillo, Liu, Nill, Paffenholz).

Ehrhart positivity is known for marked order polytopes and skew Gelfand-Tsetlin polytopes: Jochemko and Menon, arXiv:2604.08394 (2026); for Tesler polytopes only the third and fourth coefficients: Lee and Liu, Discrete Comput. Geom. (2022), arXiv:1911.06291, doi:10.1007/s00454-022-00453-1; volumes and Ehrhart polynomials of flow polytopes by Lidskii-type formulas in Kostant partition functions: Meszaros and Morales, Math. Z. (2019), arXiv:1710.00701, doi:10.1007/s00209-019-02283-z; the Ehrhart polynomials of Birkhoff polytopes for n <= 8: Beck and Pixton, arXiv:math/0202267.

Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity for rational polytopes and the constant term of the Ehrhart quasi-polynomial: Macdonald, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 4 (1971) 181-192, doi:10.1112/jlms/s2-4.1.181; Beck and Robins, 'Computing the Continuous Discretely', 2nd ed., Springer 2015, doi:10.1007/978-1-4939-2969-6.

This project, box attack attack/stretched-lr-polynomial-negative-coefficient (finished 2026-09-04): no triple of length <= 7 and size <= 30 has a negative coefficient; a proof by computation with two independent programs (Normaliz on the hive inequalities, lrcalc with exact interpolation) for length <= 6 (5,552,431 polynomials), computational evidence for length 7 (1,302,871 primitive polynomials by two encodings in one solver, plus 9,201,781 triples reduced by the factorisation theorem). Census (certified-special-case-check-4, two implementations): of the 6,855,302 computed polynomials exactly 7,469 have a coefficient below the unimodular-simplex value, all with exactly D + 1 lattice points, normalized volume 2 and h* = (1, 0, 1, 0, ...) in dimensions 4, 5, 6, minimal ratios 24/25, 44/45, 799/812; no computed polynomial with D + 1 lattice points has normalized volume above 2.

This project, negative-side attack attack/stretched-lr-negative-coefficient-unbounded (finished 2026-09-05): 453,799 sampled hive polynomials beyond the box (5 parts to size 200; 6 parts of dimension 8..10; 8 parts of dimension 3..12; 12,000 hives with at most D + 2 lattice points) and 5,170 transportation polytopes have no negative coefficient; the near-miss structure of the box recurs beyond it; at 8 parts one hive polytope with D + 1 lattice points has normalized volume 3 (lam = (4,4,3,3,2,2,1,1), mu = (3,3,2,2,1,1), nu = (3,2,2,1), c = 7, dimension 6, h* = (1, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0), minimal ratio 393/406), so the volume-2 bound is a property of length <= 7 and not of hive polytopes.

Software: Normaliz, recommended citation W. Bruns, B. Ichim, C. Soeger, U. von der Ohe, 'Normaliz. Algorithms for rational cones and affine monoids', https://www.normaliz.uni-osnabrueck.de/, version 3.11 through PyNormaliz 2.24; lrcalc 2.1 (Anders Skovsted Buch), https://math.rutgers.edu/~asbuch/lrcalc.
Mathlib has no Littlewood-Richardson coefficient and no Schur polynomial (GitHub code search of leanprover-community/mathlib4, 2026-09-03): only YoungDiagram and SemistandardYoungTableau exist.
